title: Service availability commitment sprint plan and exec summary
content:
Purpose:
Drive a focused 6-week sprint to convert the reliability program principles into a concrete availability commitment (internal SLOs + routing fallback behavior) and an operational playbook for feature teams. This doc captures scope, owners, weekly milestones, metrics, communication plan, risks, and open decisions for cross-functional partners (Product, Serving Runtime, Platform, Console, Support).

Background / Why this sprint now:
- Multiple feature launches (hosted inference upgrades + Dedicated autoscale changes) scheduled H2. We need clear SLO commitments and an operational runway to avoid surprise burns and escalations.
- Observability gaps identified: inconsistent p99 traces across models, missing categorical error tagging for cache misses and OOMs, lack of a single error-budget dashboard for leaders.
- Previous reliability efforts produced playbook drafts but not team-level rollouts. This sprint aims to finalize commitments and run a canary on one product flow.

Goals (SMART):
- Finalize service-level availability commitments for two canonical surfaces: Hosted API (text-generation/chat) and Dedicated inference pools by end of week 4. Targets: Hosted API availability 99.95% monthly, Dedicated pools 99.9% monthly (draft, subject to SLA negotiation).
- Implement and validate a single error-budget dashboard (per-route, model, and customer tier) by week 5.
- Run a canary rollout and fallback test for the hosted chat flow (region us-west) with automatic model-variant fallback and documented runbook by week 6.
- Reduce unexplained p99 latency variance >100ms incidents by 30% on the canary path.

Scope / Out of scope:
- In scope: SLO definition, metric instrumentation standardization, error-budget dashboard, canary runbook, cross-team oncall rotation adjustments for feature teams, incident playbook updates.
- Out of scope: full Dedicated contractual SLAs negotiation, on-prem appliance installation work, deep kernel-level perf optimization (will be handed to Serving Runtime backlog).

Key stakeholders and roles:
- Exec sponsor: Priya Nambiar (VP, SRE)
- Program lead / PM: Asha Mehta (SRE PM)
- Technical owner: Diego Ramirez (Serving Runtime)
- Observability lead: Martin Kwon (Platform Observability)
content_continued:
- Customer-facing docs & comms: Elena Soto (Customer Success)
- Feature-team liaisons: host-api-eng, dedicated-eng, console-product

Week-by-week milestones (6-week sprint):
Week 0 (kickoff, pre-sprint): alignment workshop, collect existing playbooks and dashboards. Deliverable: alignment notes and decision list. (owner: Asha)
Week 1: SLO proposal draft for both surfaces (metrics, window, targets, burn policy) + agreed measurement sources. Deliverable: SLO proposal doc and metric queries. (owner: Diego + Martin)
Week 2: Instrumentation fixes and tagging standard (error categories, model-tagging, route-tagging). Deliverable: instrumentation PRs and test plan. (owner: Platform Observability)
Week 3: Build error-budget dashboard (per-route + per-model) + alert burn-rate rules. Deliverable: dashboard + alerting runbook. (owner: Martin)
Week 4: Finalize availability commitments and run acceptance with stakeholders. Deliverable: signed internal SLA draft and feature-team readiness checklist. (owner: Priya + Asha)
Week 5: Canary rollout (us-west) with automated fallback and chaos test (simulated capacity pressure). Deliverable: canary runbook, run results, incident postmortem template. (owner: Diego + host-api-eng)
Week 6: Retrospective + handoff to maintenance (ops cadence, oncall rotation, runway for Dedicated SLAs). Deliverable: handoff notes, playbook in team docs. (owner: Asha)

Success criteria / acceptance tests:
- Dashboard shows correct per-route availability numbers and error categories for a 14-day test window.
- Canary run completes with automatic fallback triggered at threshold and no customer-facing errors for targeted accounts.
- Stakeholder sign-off from Product, CS, and Platform on the internal availability commitment doc.
- Three known observability gaps closed (listed in the instrument backlog) with PRs merged.

Metrics / telemetry to track:
- Availability (HTTP 200-level behavior + model-level inference errors) by route, model, region (weekly rollups and monthly aggregates).
- Latency p50/p90/p99 per route and model; track variance and tail-shift over time.
- Error budget burn rate (per route and customer tier).
- Incident count and mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for the canary path.

Communication plan / cadence:
- Weekly availability standup (30m) with stakeholders (SRE, Serving Runtime, Platform, Product). Weekly agenda: status, blockers, metrics snapshot, decisions needed. (owner: Asha)
- Daily 15m during canary week for immediate coordination. (owner: Diego)
- Mid-sprint check-in (stakeholder sync) at week 3 for signoff readiness. (owner: Priya)
- Draft customer comms and FAQ prepared by CS in week 5; Exec summary for leadership at end of week 6. (owner: Elena)

Risk heatmap (high/medium/low):
- High: Observability blind spots (missing tags, inconsistent TTL) — Mitigation: platform sprint to triage tags in week 2, require feature teams to adopt new tagging by week 3.
- High: Canary regression causes customer API errors — Mitigation: staged rollout, traffic shadowing, rollback playbook, dedicated incident bridge.
- Medium: Cross-team coordination delays (PR merges, infra quotas) — Mitigation: early unblock meeting on week 0 and clear owners for each PR.
- Low: SLA negotiation with enterprise customers drags beyond sprint — Mitigation: mark Dedicated SLA as separate track, deliver internal commitment first.

Open decisions / dependencies:
- Final availability targets (99.95% vs 99.9%) need Product + Revenue signoff (decision by end of week 4).
- Which customer accounts are included in the initial canary (need CS to nominate 3 safe customers).
- Platform quota increases for canary in us-west (infra ticket created: JIRA-INF-4399).

Runbook snippets (draft):
- If error-budget burn rate > 2x sustained for 3h: notify on #stability-ops, instantiate incident bridge, and throttle non-critical background work (owner: oncall SRE).
- If p99 latency jump > 200ms: run preflight trace collection, compare model version runtime metrics, enable KV-cache bypass for suspect model.

Action items (immediate):
- Asha: send kickoff invite + attach instrument backlog (today).
- Diego: produce SLO metric query examples and map current metric gaps (by Tue).
- Martin: prototype dashboard wire (Grafana panel + example queries) (by Fri).
- Elena: draft customer-safe canary criteria and outreach template (by end of week 1).

Appendix: artifact links and notes
- Current playbook drafts: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/availability-playbooks (linked)
- Instrumentation backlog: JIRA-INF-4300..INF-4312
- Observability standards RFC: RFC-obs-2026-02

Notes to reviewers:
- This is deliberately pragmatic: we prioritize a single observable source of truth and a canary test over polished SLA legal language. Please flag items that must be elevated (legal, security, partner commitments) ASAP so we can scope them out.
- Questions to answer in review: 1) Acceptable initial targets for Hosted vs Dedicated? 2) Will feature teams commit to tagging standard by week 3? 3) Any customer accounts that must be excluded from canary?

Next steps after signoff:
- Convert the sprint deliverables into the Console rollout checklist and a templated incident runbook per route.
- Schedule a 30-day follow-up to measure error budget drift and adjust SLOs.
